transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, you know? Like I can’t shut the motor off. It’s been getting me in trouble at the firehouse lately. Which is crazy because usually, the firehouse is the one place where being ready to go at all times is a good thing. We had this call last week, a real nasty multi-car pileup on the interstate, and the adrenaline just... well, it’s always there, but it was really pumping. I ended up organizing the whole rig’s compartments while we were waiting for the tow trucks. The captain wasn't thrilled because I was supposed to be doing traffic control, but the flares were already out, and I just couldn't stand there doing nothing. Standing still is just... it's like wearing an itchy sweater, I just can't do it. But yeah, the captain said I need to get this checked out before it becomes a real safety issue.
Did you struggle with this kind of restlessness or difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah, for sure. My mom says I was exactly like this back in grade school, too. Always out of my seat, blurting out answers, losing my homework... man, I lost so many backpacks. I remember this one time in fourth grade, I had this Ninja Turtles backpack, the one with the hard plastic shell on the back? I left it on the school bus, and the driver, Mr. Henderson—he was this older guy who used to give out those little strawberry candies with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries. Do you know the ones I'm talking about? You always see them around the holidays in fancy glass bowls but you never actually see anyone buy them in a store. I love those things, my grandma used to have them too. 

But wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, school. Yeah, I was getting notes sent home constantly. The teachers always told my mom I was bright enough to do the work, I just couldn't sit still or keep it together long enough to actually do it.

Yeah, keeping focused is... rough. Like, we have these morning briefings, or lately I've been doing this new drone training for search and rescue. I'll be totally locked in for the first few minutes, but then suddenly I realize I've just been staring at the map or the screen, and I didn't catch half of what command just said. 

Which really sucks because the drones are actually incredibly cool. We just got this new model with a thermal imaging camera on it. It’s wild what you can see with those things at night. We took it out last week over the woods near the county line, and you could see every single deer, every raccoon just glowing on the screen. Raccoons are getting massive around here, by the way. I swear I saw one by my garbage cans the other night that was the size of a golden retriever. My neighbor, Dave—he tried to trap one once because it was getting into his crawlspace, and the thing completely destroyed his trap. Just bent the metal like it was nothing. Dave was so mad, he... wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, paying attention. Yeah, I zone out a lot.
